question:
I have an incremental model in dbt that uses the data of a stream (as a source) and tries to merge into a next table.

I'm facing the problem that one of the columns is defined in the 1st table (on which the stream is created) as col_1 VARCHAR(3) and the field in the 2nd table as col_1 VARCHAR(3).

The the select statement in the model that is trying to do the merge onto the 2nd table (table_2) is set as:

SELECT
    CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(col_1, '[^\x00-\x7F]', '') AS VARCHAR(3) ) AS col_1, 
    ...
FROM
    DB.SCHEMA.stream_table_1
WHERE
    METADATA$ACTION = 'INSERT'
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...) = 1

And the DBT execution log is showing:

13:50:01 SQL status: SUCCESS 57 in 0.0 seconds 13:50:01 Changing col type from character varying(3) to character varying(16777216) in table database: "DB" schema: "SCHEMA" identifier: "table_2"
13:50:01 Using snowflake connection "model.workspace.table_2" 13:50:01 On model.workspace.table_2: /* {"app": "dbt", "dbt_version": "1.8.0", "profile_name": "but_worspace", "target_name": "qa", "node_id": "model.workspace.table_2"} */ alter table db.schema.table_2 alter "col_1" set data type character varying(16777216); 13:50:02 Snowflake adapter: Snowflake query id: 01b4587e-0105-28c1-003f-f70708b39e12

I don't know what is doing, why is an alter appearing on this?
title: DBT - Snowflake - Model trying to alter a column
answer:
In your scenario, you have created a model without any casting. Later, you've added CAST functions to the same model. In this case, your table is already created on the initial run of the model.

Running dbt run --full-refresh should fix the issue.
❗️ Please beware that it will drop your current table completely and recreate it from scratch. Generally (I'd say 99.9% of the time), you should design dbt models so you can run --full-refresh on them.

There is might be a misconception on what incremental models are for.
Incremental models:
✅ serve to optimize a dbt workload (if dbt run executes too long)
❌ do not serve to extract and load data from a streaming

Please see more details from my answer here.

dbt is responsible for the T component in the ELT (Extract, Load, Transform). It seems that you're trying to use dbt for E and L. I believe it will be highly beneficial for you if you use another tool for extracting and storing data from your streaming to the RAW database of Snowflake. And then, use view or table dbt models to transform this data for business usage.
